interview.q: Why is transition: all considered risky?
interview.answer: It animates every changing property, which can cause unexpected and janky animations.
A property that moves, rotates, scales or skews an element without affecting layout.

It rotates an element around its transform origin by a given angle.

interview.q: Why does transform not cause reflow?
interview.answer: It is a paint and composite effect applied after layout, so siblings do not move.

It moves an element in 3D space and often promotes it to its own compositing layer.

interview.q: Why use transform instead of top and left for animation?
interview.answer: Transforms are compositor-friendly and avoid layout and paint, so they are smoother.
A hint to the browser that an element will change, allowing it to prepare resources in advance.

interview.q: What is the difference between transition and animation?
interview.answer: Transitions run between two states triggered by a change; animations run keyframes on a timeline.
It fires when a transition finishes, letting JavaScript react to the completed animation.

interview.q: What happens if a property changes mid-transition?
interview.answer: The browser starts a new transition from the current intermediate value.

interview.q: What is the difference between translate and position?
interview.answer: translate moves visually without layout changes; position changes layout and flow.

interview.q: What is the difference between translate and translate3d for performance?
interview.answer: translate3d often forces GPU compositing; modern browsers treat translate similarly.
